current.text: He signed with Brooklyn for 2 years and 18 million as veteran depth. One note describes it as a mutual option deal.
He is projected as Brooklyn's sixth man, the first name in a bench rotation with Noah Clowney, Mo Wagner, Danny Wolf and Nolan Traore.
He needs about 27 minutes a game to matter in 12-team category leagues.
Treat him as a stash, not a must-roster player. Do not target him aggressively.
He can give capable minutes if Brooklyn asks him to start.

Brooklyn does not own its pick and has young players with a case for minutes. Minutes may shift to Minott, Clowney, Brown and Demin in the second half, so his role around the fantasy playoffs is uncertain.
Brooklyn plays 3-4-3 games in our playoff weeks (season ending March 28) and has 16 back-to-backs, tied for the most in the league.

durable.text: He is a low-usage wing. His fantasy value comes from steals and few turnovers. He adds little in points, rebounds and assists.

note: He ranks 257th on Yahoo and 193rd on ESPN, both sites value him at 0 USD, and he went undrafted in our league. That puts him outside the 144 players we draft, so leave him for waivers. Early in the season, check whether he gets close to the 27 minutes the experts set as his threshold. In 24.4 minutes in 2024-25 he averaged 1.5 steals and only 0.9 turnovers, so a bigger role would make him a useful steals and low-TO streamer.
